$description: NSH Gallery UI (light appearance, pointer tier) — standalone W3C DTCG 2025.10 tokens.

sharedDos: Read all colors, radii, typography, and surface finishes through theme roles (`colors.*`, `shape.*`, `font.*`, `finish.*`) rather than literals in component code.
Read theme getters inside JSX render expressions or reactive effects so runtime theme switching (`selectTheme`) and light/dark appearance changes take effect on the next frame.
Use `rounded(shape.<role>, inset)` for concentric nested radii inside cards, switches, and segmented controls.
sharedDonts: Never write color literals (`#...`, `rgb()`, `oklch()`) in component, lib, or demo-adapter code.
Never store `colors.*`, `finish.*`, or `shape.*` values in module-level constants; they freeze on theme or appearance switches.
Never delete finish fields or alter the merged finish key set across appearances or themes.
designMd.voiceOmitted: Voice & Content Strategy is intentionally omitted: this theme defines visual tokens, surface finishes, typography metrics, and motion physics only; product copy, tone, capitalization, and terminology belong to the host application.
designMd.overview: NSH Gallery UI default theme: graphite dark and paper light surfaces with citrus lime (`#c6ef6a`) brand fill, continuous squircle corners, spring motion physics, and layered surface finishes.
designMd.elevation: Tactile layered elevation: inner top-edge highlights (`inset`), 1px hairline borders, contact + cast drop shadows (`card`, `menu`, `dialog`, `inverse`), and translucent frosted glass (`glass` with 80% popover alpha).
dos: Preserve the citrus accent (`brand-fill` / `primary`) for primary actions, active runs, and focus highlights.
Use `inset` wells inside cards and `raised` surfaces for controls sitting on cards, paired with continuous squircle corners (`shape.curve: "continuous"`).
donts: Do not flatten shadows or remove inner highlights on `card`, `raised`, `inset`, or `pill` finishes.
Do not merge distinct semantic finishes (`light` vs `accent`, `thumb` vs `raised`, `knob` vs `handle`, `down` vs `destructive`).
